messages:
lee: quick heads-up — seeing a perf regression on multi-GPU TP + flash-attn when sequence-length distribution has a long tail. throughput down ~18% on our 8k->16k tail runs. attaching nsys snippet below (excerpt).

jia: can you paste the trace snippet and the exact model/config you used?

lee: model: redwood-g-3b (tp=2) runtime flags: `flash_attn=true`, `split_qkv=true`, `kv_cache_shard=per_tp`
nsys excerpt:
```
[TIMELINE] kernel: fused_flash_attn_qkv (fast path) 0.6ms
kernel: qkv_allgather (small) 0.12ms x 48
kernel: fallback_flash_attn_qkv (slow path) 3.4ms x 6
NCCL allreduce: 0.25ms x 96 (many small ops)
cudaMemcpyAsync: 0.08ms x 120
```
lee: the pattern shows lots of tiny all-gathers/allo-reduces interleaved with memcpy and occasional slow-path flash kernels. seemed fine last week on same commit.

owen: tiny NCCL ops smell like per-shard cache invalidation or non-aggregated QKV exchanges. did we change the qkv packing layout or the TP shard stride?

lee: didn't change packing, but there was a recent batching heuristic tweak: `continuous_batching=true` which lets different seq-lens mix in a batch. suspect fragmentation -> more small comms.

alex: another angle: flash-attn fallback often triggers when head dim or seq len not aligned with internal block sizes. our fallback count correlates with sequences where seq_len % 64 != 0 — those go to slow path.

jia: two possible levers to test quickly: (1) force grouped allgather for QKV to amortize comms, (2) coalesce KV cache shards before TP exchange so we do fewer bigger NCCL ops.

sam: quick repro plan: run fixed micro-bench with seq lens sampled from prod 95th/99th percentiles, run with and without `continuous_batching`, and toggle `group_qkv_allgather` and `merge_kv_shards`. measure p50/p95 token latency and NCCL op count.

lee: created short perf run: `./bench --model redwood-g-3b --tp 2 --batch 24 --seq-dist prod-tail.json --flags "flash_attn=true split_qkv=true continuous_batching=true"`
results (baseline):
```
throughput: 82 tok/s
p50 token latency: 18ms
p95 token latency: 60ms
NCCL ops per step: 96 (avg size 4KB)
```
lee: with `group_qkv_allgather=true`:
```
throughput: 95 tok/s
p50: 16ms
p95: 44ms
NCCL ops per step: 12 (avg size 32KB)
```
lee: shows most of the regression is communication overhead — grouping helps a lot.

owen: nice. how about `merge_kv_shards=true`? that should reduce memcpy churn too.

lee: ran merge_kv_shards=true + group_qkv_allgather=true:
```
throughput: 102 tok/s
p50: 15ms
p95: 40ms
NCCL ops per step: 6 (avg size 64KB)
```
lee: basically recovers and slightly improves previous baseline.

alex: good evidence. we should still understand why fallback_flash_attn_qkv triggered for some seqs — might be an upstream kernel selector bug responding to mixed sequence batches. can you capture the kernel selector inputs for the failing steps?

lee: yes, I have selector logs for a few failing steps. snippet:
```
selector: head_dim=64 seq_len=97 block=64 simd=32 arch=sm86 -> fallback
selector: head_dim=64 seq_len=128 block=64 -> fast
```
lee: odd-length sequences (like 97) push a fallback. grouping comms reduces frequency of those mixed small steps enough to hide the cost, but we probably want a proper selector fix.

jia: proposed next actions: 1) short-term opt: enable `group_qkv_allgather` + `merge_kv_shards` for TP deployments with flash-attn, 2) medium-term: update kernel selector heuristics to prefer padding or internal tiling for odd seq lens, 3) longer-term: revisit continuous_batching policy to avoid mixing very different seq lengths in same micro-batch.

sam: can we feature-flag the short-term opt for dedicated clusters? perf-bot, can you create a perf test matrix for the release branch?

perf-bot: perf-run scheduled: branch=release/optimize-comm, tests=[prod-tail, fixed-97, fixed-128], envs=[tp2-tp4], metrics=[throughput,p50,p95,nccl_count], eta=2hr.

deploy-bot: canary deploy planned for tp-dedicated pool at 2026-03-23T03:00Z with flags: `group_qkv_allgather=true,merge_kv_shards=true`. notify #eng-oncall if anomaly >10% SLA.

owen: i'll own the selector patch (will add padding heuristic and a fallback aggregation threshold). lee, can you drop the selector logs in the PR?

lee: yup, will attach logs and the micro-bench scripts.

alex: remind: check GPU kernel mem footprint after merging shards — avoid hitting L2 thrash or spilling to host. add quick `nvidia-smi dmon` snapshot to runs.

lee: will add that. thanks all — follow-up in ~3 hours with perf-bot results. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf-run complete. summary: group_qkv_allgather + merge_kv_shards restores baseline and reduces p95 by ~33% on prod-tail. selector-patch branch in review.
